business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal jurisdiction; target seat and cantonal registry to be designated at notarization, e.g., Zug, Zurich, or Geneva)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified by the Swiss Civil Code, Code of Obligations, and federal statutes; cantonal procedural variations; direct-democratic referenda and customary elements create a hybrid institutional overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 12 November 1986, as amended by the Protocol of 27 April 2010)
China - Switzerland Free Trade Agreement (in force since 1 July 2014, negotiated within the EFTA framework)
Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation between Switzerland and the United States of America (signed 2 October 1996, as amended by the protocols of 2009 and 2012)
Switzerland - United Kingdom Trade Agreement and double-taxation arrangement (applied from 1 January 2021)
Switzerland - Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1971, as amended by the 1971/2010 protocols)
EFTA Convention (Vaduz, 21 June 2001) and EFTA free trade agreements with Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, Canada, and Chile

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG/AMLA; SR 955.0, 10 October 1997, as amended, in particular Art. 2a, 3, 6-8); Implementing Ordinance on Money Laundering (GwV/AMLO; SR 955.01, 11 November 2015, as amended, and FINMA AML Ordinance-CDB 20/03); Code of Obligations (OR; SR 220) Art. 626-628 imposing a mandatory internal register of beneficial owners for all Swiss legal entities; Swiss Criminal Code (StGB; SR 311.0) Art. 305bis, 305ter, and 260quinquies; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV; SR 221.411) and cantonal notarial deed requirements; SECO sanctions ordinances (SR 946.201 ff.) implementing UN, EU/CFSP, and OFAC-aligned restrictive measures; Banking Act Art. 3 licensing thresholds considered but not expected to be triggered by delivery-only kitchen operations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current commercial register extract / business registry report of each foreign corporate shareholder or ultimate corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or Registrar of Companies in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified true-copy of the passport or national identity card of each founder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner (natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin; alternatively the consular section of the Swiss representation at the UBO's place of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, non-bankruptcy, criminal-record extract, and tax-clearance certificate for each UBO and corporate shareholder, where legally obtainable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court, insolvency registry, or tax authority of the UBO's country of domicile

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth and source of funds declaration (AML statement) covering the share-capital deposit, with notarized signature of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of origin; if attested in Switzerland, a Swiss notary instead

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Blocked-account (Sperrkonto) bank confirmation issued by a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank evidencing deposit of the minimum share capital (CHF 100,000; 20% paid-up and at least CHF 50,000 in cash)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank holding the incorporation escrow account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization not required; the bank signature is verified by the Swiss notary in the course of the public deed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed in favor of the Swiss incorporation agent or attorney, with grantor identity and capacity attested
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the grantor's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC screening must be performed immediately before incorporation and on any subsequent issuance or transfer event: (i) Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) enforced sanctions list and all Swiss federal sanctions ordinances (SR 946.201-946.230, incorporating UN and EU/CFSP measures); (ii) US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (v) PEP list and sectoral guidance under FINMA AML Ordinance-CDB 20/03; (vi) World Bank, EBRD, and ADB debarment registers. Any PEP, PEP relative, or close associate triggers enhanced due diligence and, where a sanctions hit is confirmed, mandatory termination of the incorporation engagement. Screening results must be archived in the company's KYC file and made available to MROS, FINMA, cantonal authorities, and the commercial register upon statutory request. Refresh frequency is six months or upon any trigger event, applying GwG diligence duties and FINMA Circular 2023/03.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), https://www.zefix.ch, operated under the Swiss Federal Register Ordinance; the formal name reservation is requested through a notary at the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the company's intended seat; the register entry is later filed via the same authority with the public deed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 944-950 of the Code of Obligations, the name must not be misleading and must permit registration in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian; Romansh admissible in limited cases). Latin script is mandatory for the registered company name; foreign-language names, including English or transliterated Chinese, are admissible provided a clear translation into a Swiss official language is recorded in the articles of association and the trade name does not create deceptive associations with regulated gastronomy or food-safety terms absent the corresponding license. The juridical suffix must be expressed in a Swiss official language: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German), 'Société anonyme' or 'SA' (French), 'Società anonima' or 'SA' (Italian); a secondary-language alias may be filed. For delivery-only virtual brands, the statutory name should remain clearly distinct from each delivery marketplace handle (e.g., Uber Eats, DoorDash) to avoid consumer confusion under the Swiss Unfair Competition Act.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swissness references: 'Schweiz', 'Swiss', 'Suisse', 'Svizzera', 'Eidgenossenschaft', 'Confédération' where the company does not satisfy the criteria of Art. 47 Trade Mark Protection Act (MSchG), requiring prior authorization of the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI)
Banking terms: 'Bank', 'Banque', 'Banca', 'Kredit' absent a Banking Act (BankA) license or authorized statutory exemption
Insurance terms: 'Versicherung', 'Assurance', 'Assicurazione' absent the insurance supervisory license
State and public authority references: 'Bundesrat', 'Nationalrat', 'Ständerat', 'Kanton', 'Bund', 'Bundesverwaltung', 'Zoll', 'Post', 'Polizei' - generally excluded or requiring official concession
Regulated financial terms: 'Fonds', 'Fund', 'Asset Management', 'Anlageberatung' where FINMA licensing or registration under the CISA/CIS cannot be evidenced
Misleading gastronomy references: 'Restaurant', 'Bistro', 'Kitchen', 'Chef' where the entity itself does not hold the operational food-safety permit for the delivery-only kitchen site
Geographic place names of cities or cantons without a genuine local establishment at that place, per Art. 946-947 OR and case law on misleading territorial indications

Generic superlatives: 'International', 'Holding', 'Group', 'Global' where the actual corporate structure does not support the term; 'Holding' requires predominant equity-participation function consistent with Swiss tax and company-law practice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The notary shall first obtain a cantonal preliminary name examination (Vorabklärung), which reserves the approved name for 90 days pending the notarized deed. If the name is rejected, the notary or counsel may immediately re-submit a corrected name without an additional order in the same canton. To contest a formal negative decision of the commercial register, the founder must file a written administrative complaint with the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority (kantonale Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) within 30 days of written notification, stating legal grounds and attaching a revised draft of the articles; where rejection relies on Swissness rules (Art. 47 MSchG), an advance ruling from the IPI should be obtained before re-filing. After the cantonal supervisory avenue is exhausted, recourse lies with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) under Art. 82 ff. of the Federal Supreme Court Act (BGG), to be filed within 30 days of the cantonal decision. The negative determination does not preclude a fresh name submission after 90 days without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Swiss AG must maintain a registered office (Sitz) in the canton stated in its articles; the Commercial Register accepts a 'c/o' or care-of address at a licensed Swiss fiduciary, corporate-services, or attorney office if postal reachability and physical availability are contractually secured. A fully letterbox-only address without any Swiss operational nexus is not sufficient for an active delivery-only ghost-kitchen operator. The recommended structure combines a registered office at a virtual-office service provider with a leased or owned licensed kitchen facility in Switzerland, plus a Swiss bank account, Swiss bookkeeping, and administration actually managed from the seat. For treaty protection and corporate substance, the effective place of management (tatsächliche Verwaltung) must be in Switzerland; a purely foreign-managed letterbox entity risks re-domiciliation or denial of tax residence benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Moderate. Unannounced physical inspections at the registered office by the Commercial Register or the Federal Tax Administration occur in fewer than 2% of newly incorporated AGs per calendar year, except where red flags appear such as serial registrations, cross-border UBO concentration, or declared virtual-business models. The cantonal food-safety authority will conduct unannounced hygiene and operational inspections at the actual kitchen site, with an estimated 60-80% probability of at least one inspection within any two-year operating window for delivery-only kitchens. The cantonal VAT office may additionally undertake a documentary substance audit within the first 18 months, with an estimated 15-25% likelihood for entities relying on marketplace payouts (UberEats/DoorDash) or cross-border brand licensing; the inspection risk profile nonetheless remains standard for this ISIC 5610 business scope.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register registration fee (federal settlement plus cantonal terminal fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (Gebührenverordnung zum Handelsregister, SR 221.411); CHF 600 federal base plus minor cantonal surcharge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability preliminary examination (Vorabklärung) through notary and Zefix
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing cantonal tariff CHF 150-300 per name-check request

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of statutory documents and UBO certificates into the register language (German, French, or Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal sworn translation office or certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Swiss market benchmark CHF 80-120 per standard page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated Apostille authority of the document-issuing state and, where required, Swiss diplomatic or consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed administrative tariffs under Art. 3 of the Hague Apostille Convention; CHF 40-120 per document plus courier costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; SR 220), Articles 620-763 governing the Aktiengesellschaft (AG); formation and capital provisions under Articles 629-632; corporate governance under Articles 707-726.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons), with federal coordination through the Swiss Commercial Register Electronic System (eGRIS) and the Zefix central name index.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Official Application for Registration of a Stock Corporation (Anmeldung zur Eintragung der Aktiengesellschaft im Handelsregister), accompanied by the public deed of incorporation and the Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum registered share capital is CHF 100,000. Before registration, at least 20% of the nominal share capital, but not less than CHF 50,000, must be fully paid in and deposited in a blocked bank account (gesperrtes Bankkonto) in the name of the company; the blocked funds are released only after the Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Articles of Association are ratified and all issued shares are subscribed by the founders. The paid-up capital has been deposited in a blocked bank account as required by Swiss law and will be at the disposal of the company after registration. (2) The registered office of the company is adopted at the place indicated in the Articles of Association and is fixed for the purposes of legal notice. (3) The directors listed in the founding declaration are appointed, with individual signatory authority, to act and represent the company. (4) The Board of Directors is authorized to complete the commercial register filing, engage notaries and advisors, and take all steps necessary to obtain all required cantonal food-trade and environmental permits for the delivery-only cloud kitchen operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and preparation of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office; federal name index Zefix via the official Swiss Commercial Register portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search Zefix for identical or deceptively similar company names; reserve the selected name; draft the Articles of Association (Statuten) preparing the corporate name, seat, purpose including delivery-only cloud kitchen and virtual brands, share capital, number and type of shares, board structure, and auditors. Execute the share subscription list and convene the inaugural shareholders' meeting for the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Zefix name reservation confirmation
Draft Articles of Association
Founders' valid identification (passport or Swiss identity card)
Share subscription list with number of shares subscribed
Power of attorney for each founder if represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, select an alternative name and update the Articles accordingly; the reservation process can be restarted within one business day on the same portal without forfeiture of the filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of share capital and blocked bank account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank authorized by FINMA or a Swiss branch of a recognized foreign bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital contribution account (Sperrkonto) in the company's future name; pay in at least CHF 50,000 as the statutory minimum paid-up capital. Instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate (Blockierungsbestätigung) confirming that the funds are at the entire disposal of the company only upon its registration in the Commercial Register. Provide a release instruction template to be executed after registration.
required_dossiers: Founders' identification documents and corporate information
Draft Articles of Association
Bank's economic purpose declaration and source of funds form
Signature specimen of contributors or their authorized representatives
Bank account opening mandate signed by all future shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide supplementary source-of-funds documentation such as tax records and constituent ownership declarations; if cash capital is rejected, convert the contribution into a non-cash contribution (Sacheinlage) supported by an independent audit report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation, commercial register filing and publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public and the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the public deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) and the foundation report before the Swiss notary. Submit the notarised application to the Cantonal Commercial Register with all required attachments. Upon scrutiny, the registry effects the registration and automatically publishes the formation excerpt in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsblatt).
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
Signed Articles of Association
Foundation report with confirmations on share subscriptions and payments
Bank blocking certificate for paid-up capital
Certified identification and signature cards of the Board of Directors
Written declaration by the board accepting their mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query, respond in writing within the statutory deadline and supply the missing documents; any notarial defect may be cured by an additional notarial declaration and the application can be resubmitted without restarting the formation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal food trade license for ghost kitchen operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal food safety authority (Kantonales Lebensmittelinspektorat / Kantonschemiker) in cooperation with the cantonal veterinary and food control office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the delivery-only cloud kitchen as a food business under the Federal Foodstuffs Ordinance (LMV) and the Food Hygiene Ordinance (HyV). Submit the floor plan, HACCP plan, menu categories, allergen management procedures, and a declaration that all food is prepared for delivery only. The cantonal authority may inspect the premises before issuing the operating permit.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt of the newly incorporated AG
Floor plan and ventilation plan of the kitchen and packing area
HACCP food safety plan
Allergen and cross-contamination control procedure
Waste and grease disposal contracts
Proof of food handler training for responsible personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the food authority requires corrective measures, complete the construction, hygiene, or process changes and request a re-inspection; temporary refusal may be cured and the license issued once the premises meet the official food hygiene protocol.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, fire safety and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal environmental protection authority (Umweltschutzfachstelle), cantonal fire safety authority (Feuerpolizei / Gebäudeversicherung), and Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the environmental self-declaration for the kitchen facility covering wastewater, fat separators, exhaust air, and waste handling; obtain the fire safety certificate for the commercial kitchen, including verification of extinguishing systems, escape routes, and building fire load; register the workplace and employees with Suva for accident insurance and occupational safety supervision.
required_dossiers: Environmental self-declaration and greasy wastewater separator plan
Kitchen exhaust and ventilation compliance certificate
Fire safety inspection protocol and fire load calculation
Building occupancy certificate for the commercial unit
Suva employer registration confirmation and accident insurance policy
Electrical installation inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any non-compliance identified in fire, environmental, or occupational inspection reports and provide photographic or architect's certification of the remedial works; if a major environmental impact is identified, a limited EIA screening procedure may be initiated, but for standard ghost kitchens this remains a registration-only pathway.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and Cantonal Tax Administration; cantonal compensation office (Ausgleichskasse).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the AG for value added tax (VAT) with ESTV if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 250,000; obtain the canton tax number; register as an employer with the cantonal old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV) compensation office and submit the employer form for social security and occupational accident insurance.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
Board of Directors' identification documents
Projected annual turnover and revenue model for delivery platforms
Employer declaration and list of initial employees
Corporate address and postal address for tax notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority issues a late-registration penalty or query, provide a voluntary disclosure with supporting turnover projections; amend the employer registration and pay any late social security contributions as part of a settlement to avoid escalation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) acting jointly with the Cantonal Food Safety and Veterinary Authority and the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal Food Trade and Operating Permit for Delivery-Only Cloud Kitchen / Virtual Brand Production Unit (Bewilligung für den Betrieb einer Take-Away-/Kurier-Küche mit virtuellen Marken).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN), with execution and enforcement by the Cantonal Environmental Protection Authority (Kantonale Umweltschutzfachstelle).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / self-declaration category; mandatory full EIA is not triggered for a standard low-capacity ghost kitchen, although a facultative EIA screening can be required if the facility is attached to a large delivery hub or has unusually high air-emission or wastewater loads.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for wastewater quality, including grease separator capacity requirements and pH limits; compliance with the Clean Air Act and the VOC Ordinance (LRV) for kitchen exhaust air, particularly maximum workplace and emission limit values for cooking fumes and volatile organic compounds; waste handling in accordance with the Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA) and provincial waste management plans.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the cantonal fire protection authority (Brandschutzbescheinigung), including structural load inspection, means of escape, extinguishing systems, and kitchen exhaust fire suppression; occupational safety and health clearance from Suva confirming workplace risk assessment and accident prevention provisions; building occupancy certificate confirming commercial use; electrical installation and mechanical ventilation clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV / AFC) of the Swiss Confederation, VAT Division; operational portal at www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that is not established in Switzerland but undertakes an economic activity in Switzerland must submit the official Swiss VAT registration application (Form 103) to the Federal Tax Administration, including the legal form, business purpose, projected Swiss turnover, and the contact details of a Swiss fiscal representative if required. Upon approval, the FTA issues a Swiss VAT identification number (MWST/TVA/IVA) and assigns a tax period and reporting obligation. The applicant must also register for foreign entity direct tax purposes with the cantonal tax administration of the place of business, if any, and, in the absence of an establishment, no direct tax registration is generally required unless treaty-qualified permanent establishment nexus arises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available. Swiss statutory law classifies an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) as a corporate taxpayer resident in Switzerland subject to federal, cantonal, and communal profit tax on its worldwide income, subject to treaty-based relief for foreign permanent establishments and real estate. The AG may elect, under Article 21 of the Swiss VAT Act, to form a VAT group with wholly controlled Swiss group entities, thereby treating the group as one taxable person for VAT purposes. Certain Swiss group financing, participation, and R&D super deductions require statutory elections or disclosure on the tax return. Hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed by Swiss law implementing the OECD Hybrid Mismatch Rules, with no elective deviation from those rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual turnover from taxable supplies and services, excluding exempt supplies, for Swiss-resident businesses; CHF 250,000 annual turnover from Swiss-source services for non-resident businesses without an establishment in Switzerland; separate CHF 100,000 threshold applies to distance-selling and marketplace facilitators; reduced CHF 20,000 threshold for small non-profit, charitable, or public-interest entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory government real-time tax clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control regime exists. Invoicing must comply with Swiss VAT invoice content rules, including supplier and recipient identification, VAT rate, amount of VAT, and transaction date. Domestic and cross-border invoices must adopt the Swiss QR-bill standard where payment is made by Swiss bank transfer, and export declarations must be lodged electronically through the Swiss customs system (e-dec / SWISS-PRODEC). There is no mandatory API clearance layer beyond the customs export declaration and periodic VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Switzerland to a non-Swiss destination are zero-rated when the vendor proves that ownership has passed to the foreign buyer and that the goods have actually left the Swiss customs territory. Services are zero-rated for exported use, including consultancy, digital services, catering and food supply services used wholly outside Switzerland, and services physically rendered abroad. The ghost kitchen must maintain evidence of the foreign customer relationship, delivery to the foreign destination, and the actual receipt of payment from outside Switzerland. Proof of export must be preserved in the ordinary course of business and made available to the Federal Tax Administration upon request.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrschein / Exportschein) or Swiss electronic export summary with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or equivalent transport document showing departure from Switzerland and arrival abroad
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice / SWIFT confirmation evidencing payment transfer from the foreign buyer to the Swiss seller account
Commercial invoice and delivery note referencing the exported goods and the underlying ghost kitchen order
Written contract or purchase order from the non-resident customer proving the offshore commercial relationship
Proof of foreign customs clearance, if applicable (such as import declaration in the destination country)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT authorities scrutinize export zero-rating claims through documentary audits and cross-border information exchange. If the exporter cannot furnish the prescribed export pack within the statutory retention period, the zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back, VAT becomes due at 8.1% with default interest, and administrative fines of up to three times the evaded tax may be imposed. Where false or forged export documentation is used to obtain an unjustified VAT advantage, criminal prosecution may follow under Article 80 of the Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax, with penalties up to 3 times the tax evaded, and, in severe cases, imprisonment; the limitations period for tax evasion and VAT fraud is 10 years, and for minor negligence claims 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank, SR 951.11) acting both as the central monetary authority and as the operator of the SIC clearing system and CHF settlement accounts; complemented by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking and AML regulation under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (SR 955.0) and the Financial Services Act (FinSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility without a general FX permit regime. Switzerland maintains a liberalised current and capital account under Federal Constitution Art. 27 (economic freedom) and the National Bank Act; there are no exchange control restrictions on capital inflows, equity subscriptions, intercompany loans, or current-account payments. Profit remittance is unrestricted by the SNB, but outbound dividends attract a statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer, SR 642.21) which is fully refundable under the domicile principle or partially reclaimable under an applicable double tax treaty. Actual convertibility of the CHF is unencumbered; the SNB intervenes in FX markets only for monetary-policy price stability, not for convertibility rationing. The sole constraints on cross-border flows derive from the international sanctions framework (Embargo Act, SR 946.231.1) under which payments to sanctioned jurisdictions or persons are frozen and reported to SECO.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no fixed repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Cross-border trading income from ghost-kitchen delivery services, brand licensing, and international consulting fees may be held indefinitely in any convertible currency. The only binding obligations are statistical and AML-related: (i) SNB balance-of-payments reporting (ZIVAP/SNO-Gen) once cumulative annual cross-border payments exceed CHF 500,000 requiring monthly electronic filing of transaction-level data with the SNB; and (ii) FINMA AMLA diligence for all cash transactions in excess of CHF 100,000 per counter-party, which is inapplicable to the digital payout rails of UberEats and DoorDash but relevant for potential cash reconciliation in commissary procurement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (CHF, EUR, USD) with SWIFT GPI, plus separate Capital Escrow Account for the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital and AMLA-compliant source-of-funds verification
Operational account with SIC and SEPA rails, dedicated sub-ledger for brand-level payout reconciliation; suitable for high-volume platform settlements
Operational multi-currency account for EU/UK supplier disbursements; commercial LC issuance desk via SWIFT MT700
Operational account with low transaction tariffs and instant CHF SIC transfers; subsidiary payment sleeve only, not for FX or LC operations
Operational account for CHF-denominated payroll and kitchen-lease rent disbursements in cantonal branches

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low as a primary treasury rail; viable only as a peripheral disbursement sleeve. Legal constraints: (i) EEA-authorised e-money institutions (e.g., Lithuania-licensed or UK FCA EMIs) cannot passport money-remittance or e-money services into Switzerland without FINMA authorisation; their use is limited to payouts into foreign delivery partners and EU suppliers, not for CHF custody or capital escrow; (ii) any FinTech EMI holding CHF on behalf of the AG requires a Swiss banking licence or FinTech licence under Art. 1b Banking Act, with a hard CHF 1 million sight-deposit cap; (iii) FINMA-regulated Swiss digital banks (e.g., Yapeal, Alpian, Radicant) permit remote video-KYC onboarding under FINMA Circular 2020/05, but capital-escrow accumulation above CHF 1 million is prohibited, forcing the use of UBS/ZKB for the share-capital deposit. Recommended architecture: UBS/ZKB core settlement accounts plus a single GBP-denominated EMI sleeve for UK-side UberEats/DoorDash payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks permit remote onboarding for the individual legal representative using a FINMA-approved video-identification procedure (e.g., SwissID, Swisscom Identity) under AMLA-Circular 2020/05. However, for an AG with non-resident shareholders and a CHF 2 million-plus capital injection, at least one executive director with signatory authority must appear physically at the bank's Zurich/Geneva/Lugano branch to execute the statutory signature card and activate high-limit electronic banking permissions. Second-tier cantonal banks typically require an in-person interview for foreign-domiciled beneficial owners; remote-onboarding approval time is 3-5 weeks versus 2-3 weeks with a physical visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-revenue capital injection with no operating history and no physical restaurant assets owned by the AG
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share-subscription list, Swiss notary deposit receipt, audited 90-day cash-flow forecast, executed kitchen-lease agreement for the licensed commissary, unit-economics model per virtual brand, and source-of-funds statements of all subscribing shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple virtual brand trade names operating under one legal entity - mismatch between commercial registry name and brand identities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCTE/IPI trademark registration certificates for each virtual brand, brand licensing agreements between the AG and the brand-holding SPV, complete list of delivery-platform merchant account IDs, and the Handelsregister excerpt evidencing DBA registrations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value settlement flows from delivery aggregators (UberEats, DoorDash, Just Eat) resembling layering patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month payout statements per platform, signed platform partner agreements, monthly reconciliation reports of platform net revenue versus VAT (Swiss MWST) and income tax accruals, plus audit log from the cloud-kitchen management system (POS/Order Management) demonstrating end-to-end settlement matching.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors with mixed tax residencies creating beneficial-ownership opacity under AMLA Art. 4
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates from each director's domicile state, passport copies, signed AMLA Form C (beneficial owner declaration), certificate of non-pending bankruptcy from the domicile jurisdiction, and the full board resolution appointing the Swiss-resident authorised signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume cross-currency conversions between USD/EUR/CHF and basket-currency payments to foreign food and packaging suppliers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supplier framework contracts quoting foreign-currency prices, cross-border payable ledger extract, board-approved treasury and FX hedging policy, and a reference letter (MT199) from the principal supplier's bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol for the CHF equity capital: the subscribing shareholder sends a SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pain.001 from a bank account registered in the shareholder's corporate name to the AG's blocked capital-escrow account at UBS/ZKB, citing the SNB balance-of-payments purpose code for foreign direct investment equity (category 'other direct investment - equity capital'), and including the UETR for SWIFT GPI tracking. The transfer is held for a 2-business-day FINMA frozen-funds verification window, then released upon the notary's confirmation. For intercompany shareholder loans exceeding CHF 1 million, an additional signed loan agreement with arm's-length interest, a board resolution, and a dedicated purpose-code designation for 'intercompany financing' must be retained for SNB statistical reporting and for cantonal capital tax assessment. No FINMA prior approval is required for the injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) CHF payments within Switzerland and Liechtenstein using SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) with instant finality, used for kitchen rent and payroll; (ii) EUR disbursements to EU suppliers and warehouse operators via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with full IBAN, settled through EBA Clearing; (iii) USD and non-EEA settlements via SWIFT MT103 with a correspondent bank chain, mandatory for US food-ingredient importers and Asian packaging vendors; (iv) for high-value procurement contracts above CHF 500,000 an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit is issued via UBS using SWIFT MT700, with conforming documents presented under MT707 amendments; (v) platform payouts from UberEats and DoorDash arrive as aggregated daily or weekly settlement batches via Adyen/Braintree into the multi-currency account, requiring automated reconciliation against platform settlement reports and delivery-fee tax certificates; (vi) repatriation of profits to the parent is treated as a dividend under Swiss withholding-tax rules and must be executed via SWIFT MT103 with tax payment proof to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC currency forward contracts with the core Swiss bank (tenors 1-24 months, collateral margin 3-7% for CHF/EUR/USD), permitted under Swiss treasury law without exchange-control approval

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market settlement currencies (TRY, BRL, MXN, IDR) where an onshore CHF-deliverable market is absent - executable through UBS/ZKB global FX desks with ISDA Master Agreement
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for USD/CHF and EUR/CHF with tenors of 1-5 years, used to hedge the structural mismatch arising from CHF equity funding and USD/EUR platform-payout receivables
FX options (long positions only, premium strategy) capped at 1.5% of hedged notional to preserve upside on EUR receivables volatility, cleared bilaterally with the relationship bank
Currency basis-swap overlay (EURIBOR vs SOFR) to neutralise the EUR/USD basis risk embedded in the Euro-area and US delivery-payout portfolios

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report presented to the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the AGM; no governmental registration required for a non-listed AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the financial year end in accordance with Swiss Code of Obligations (OR 699)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of OR 700; civil liability of the board; judicial convocation of AGM upon shareholder petition; persistent non-organization can trigger administrative strike-off pursuant to Civil Code art. 731b after due notice and public warning.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal, cantonal and municipal corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the fiscal year end; extensions may be granted by the cantonal tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at the statutory rate, procedural penalties up to 30% of the evaded tax, estimated assessments, fines, and enforced collection; continued absence of achievable tax filings may evidence defective organization and lead to strike-off procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer social security wage statement (AHV/AVS declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office (FSIO) through the competent cantonal equalization fund
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of the calendar year following the wage reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contribution arrears interest, administrative fines up to 5% of unpaid contributions, and debt enforcement under the Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return, where an annual accounting period is elected or prescribed by the FTA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within sixty (60) days after the end of the annual tax period; quarterly periods are generally due 60 days after the quarter end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest, VAT administrative penalties under Article 60 of the VAT Act, compulsory tax assessment, debt collection proceedings, and potential deletion from the VAT register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full ordinary audit applies to companies exceeding two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, and 250 full-time employees; publicly listed companies and entities required by law or articles are always subject to full ordinary audit. A limited audit is required for companies exceeding CHF 10 million balance-sheet total, CHF 20 million turnover, or 50 employees. Companies below these small-company limits may dispense with an audit only if all shareholders consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting provisions; Swiss GAAP FER for SME-oriented financial statements; IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER mandatory for listed companies under the SIX Swiss Exchange regulatory requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not maintain a central public UBO annual confirmation filing. The company must identify beneficial owners on an ongoing basis under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, and the share register must be updated immediately upon any share transfer. The annual share-register inventory reviewed at the AGM functions as the de facto annual confirmation of shareholding. Any changes requiring public registrability, such as restructuring or significant changes of control, must be filed with the Commercial Register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 800 – CHF 2,500 (approximately USD 900 – USD 2,800) per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit fee for a small AG that validly waives audit; limited audit typically CHF 3,000 – CHF 7,000 (approximately USD 3,300 – USD 7,800); full ordinary audit typically CHF 10,000 – CHF 30,000 (approximately USD 11,000 – USD 33,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal proportional corporate income tax; plus cantonal/communal CIT resulting in aggregate headline rates from 11.9% (Zug) to 21.0% (Zurich) depending on the registered office
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general Swiss statutory tax holiday; limited cantonal innovation reliefs apply (e.g. patent box allowing up to 90% exemption of IP income, R&D super-deduction up to 50%); these are irrelevant for a standard delivery-only multi-brand ghost kitchen unless proprietary virtual-brand IP or food-tech patents are exploited

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal unified direct-tax declaration for legal entities (e.g. Zurich Form StF 30, Geneva TaxMe); submitted electronically through the relevant cantonal tax authority and synchronised with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) e-filing portal; Swiss UID number mandatory
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the tax-relevant financial year-end; for a calendar-year AG the ordinary deadline is 30 June, with extensions available upon written request; cantonal variations apply

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Swiss Company Register number, UID, registered seat, legal form, fiscal representative details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not directly entered on the return; the company must identify its ultimate beneficial owner in the shareholder disclosure annex; the AG remains the resident taxpayer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities and equity per audited commercial accounts; reconcile any undisclosed reserves and latent reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Equity portion attributable to non-resident investors is entered without distinction; only Swiss situs assets and working capital affect Swiss taxation years

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, food-delivery platform commissions, raw material COGS, staff costs, rent, utility expenses, depreciation, operating profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Swiss-source and worldwide income of the AG must be declared; foreign-owned virtual brands must retain invoices for royalty or franchise payments to third parties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corrections to commercial profit: non-deductible expenses, tax provisions, transfer-pricing adjustments, patent-box allocation, participation relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If intercompany fees are paid to non-resident affiliated virtual-brand owners, enter them as separately-disclosed related-party transactions and attach transfer-pricing documentation on request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, deemed profit OR, interest on bonds and bank deposits paid to shareholders and creditors; reserved for the Swiss 35% withholding tax and DTA relief procedures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Swiss Tax Administration forms (85, 93 or 852) and each beneficial owner's tax residence certificate when reduced DTA rates are claimed; failure to file exposes the AG to default withholding liability

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing attracts procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 per breach, default interest on unpaid assessments at approx. 4.5% p.a., and possible interim third-party assessment; willful false declarations constitute tax evasion and are punished separately

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (Swiss federal withholding tax, Verrechnungssteuer, on gross dividend distributions)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA reduction or elimination: (1) file claim with the Federal Tax Administration using official FTA withholding-tax forms (e.g. Form 85 for refund, Form 852 for advance exemption); (2) obtain a valid tax-residence certificate (TRC) from the beneficial owner's national tax authority; (3) confirm no treaty shopping through substantive economic activity; (4) in some cantons, obtain prior approval of reduced rate through a notification procedure; refund claims are due within three years after the calendar year of distribution
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no statutory Swiss WHT on pure licence or royalty payments; DTA rates range 0–10% for treaty countries. Interest: no WHT on ordinary intercompany loan interest; only Swiss tax-relevant bond and bank-deposit interest triggers the 35% federal WHT, with DTA reductions generally to 10% or 0% (for certain parent-subsidiary loans)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold in Swiss law; Federal Tax Administration practice requires Local File documentation when related-party cross-border transactions involve material amounts (commonly interpreted above CHF 3,000,000 per annum) or when inter-group financing exceeds CHF 1,000,000; Master File/CbCR is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue over CHF 900,000,000; ordinary documentation must be available within 30 days upon tax authority request
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations as found in offshore jurisdictions do not apply to Switzerland; however, the Swiss anti-treaty-abuse doctrine and OECD BEPS rules require actual business substance (office, staff, active decision-making, physical kitchen operations); a letterbox AG being used for passive profit-shifting will have DTA benefits denied, profits recomputed, and possibly 35% WHT triggered on deemed distributions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful or grossly negligible omission of taxable income, deliberately false books, fictitious expenses, and sham transfer-pricing invoices orchestrated to reduce Swiss CIT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 50% of the tax evaded (simple), up to 100% or more in qualified cases, plus default interest and reassessment; Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax imposes fines up to ten times the evaded amount where extraordinary culpability is shown; illegal asset seizure and confiscation of criminal proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and shadow directors who sign false tax returns or instruct concealment are criminally liable; imprisonment for up to 5 years is possible; personal net worth may be attached for tax restitution and procedural fines; travel bans can be imposed during criminal investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a Swiss AG with no substantial ghost-kitchen operations, no personnel, no leased premises, and allowing foreign parent to control delivery contracts while profits accumulate under the AG merely to obtain DTA residency benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of profits to the foreign actual entrepreneurial benefactor, denial of treaty benefits, added assessed income subject to CIT at combined rates, deemed-dividend treatment and assessment of 35% WHT if economic substance refutation is sustained
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Formal directors who knowingly participate in shell-company structures may be jointly and severally liable for deficient withholding taxes; criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion and failure to take mandated bankruptcy measures; in extreme cases they can be imprisoned and banned from acting as directors in Switzerland

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or deemed benefits to foreign shareholders without applying the 35% Swiss withholding tax; refunds taken for fictitious treaty residence certificates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal withholding tax assessed as a direct claim against the company, default interest from due date, penalty of up to 100% of unpaid tax; if the foreign shareholder becomes unreachable, the AG remains liable for the gross amount
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for wilful non-deduction of withholding tax and social-security deductions; their salary and seizure orders and, in serious cases, criminal imprisonment up to three years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ghost-kitchen cash receipts not banked, using anonymous payment rails, clearing delivery-platform payouts to third-party personal wallets, or knowingly accepting proceeds of tax evasion or fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Position not a licensed Swiss financial intermediary for ordinary restaurant collection; however, if the AG enters into lending, payment processing or arranged crypto-currency payouts, the Anti-Money Laundering Act applies; administrative fines up to CHF 500,000 and possible revocation of banking permission; supervisory sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to report suspicious transactions under the GwG/AMLA can be prosecuted for money laundering (StGB Art. 305bis); imprisonment up to three years, up to 5 when acting as criminal organisation member; personal bans from holding office and asset freezing orders
